destinations.name: Bandarban
destinations.description: Bandarban is a hill district famous for its misty peaks, tribal culture, and lush valleys, offering some of the most scenic trekking routes in Bangladesh.
destinations.weather_notes: Cool and dry in winter; heavy monsoon rain June-September
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Hill resorts and cottages in Nilgiri/Milanchari area
destinations.travel_tips: Carry warm clothing for early morning hill viewpoints; roads can be steep and winding
destinations.permits_required: Special permit required for Thanchi, Ruma and deep hill-tract routes

destinations.name: Cox's Bazar
destinations.description: Cox's Bazar offers an unbroken 120km sandy beach along with island getaways like Saint Martin and Inani.
destinations.weather_notes: Warm and dry in winter; rough seas and monsoon rains June-September
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Beachfront hotels along Marine Drive and Kolatoli
destinations.travel_tips: Sunrise at Sugandha Point and sunset at Laboni Point are must-sees
destinations.permits_required: None for the mainland beach; NOC required for Saint Martin during restricted seasons

destinations.name: Rangamati
destinations.description: Rangamati sits on the shores of Kaptai Lake, offering boat rides, hanging bridges, and indigenous Chakma culture.
destinations.weather_notes: Warm days, cool evenings in winter; heavy rainfall in monsoon
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Lake-view resorts and floating cottages near the hanging bridge
destinations.travel_tips: Book a boat early for a full-day Kaptai Lake and Shuvolong tour
destinations.permits_required: ID verification required for some restricted zones

destinations.name: Sajek Valley
destinations.description: Sajek Valley is situated in the north of Chittagong Hill Tracts, surrounded by lush green mountains and drifting clouds with breathtaking panoramic viewpoints.
destinations.weather_notes: Crisp and misty in morning; sea of clouds visible throughout monsoon and autumn
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Eco-cottages and wooden mountain resorts along Ruilui Ridge
travelTips: Reach Dighinala military convoy point before 10 AM or 3 PM
Bring power bank as electricity can be intermittent
destinations.permits_required: Convoy escort mandatory from Dighinala to Sajek

destinations.name: Sylhet
destinations.tagline: Land of Two Leaves and a Bud
destinations.description: Sylhet is home to rolling green tea gardens, crystalline freshwater springs like Jaflong, and the mystical Ratargul freshwater swamp forest.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: June to October for waterfalls and swamps; November to March for tea gardens
destinations.weather_notes: Highest rainfall in Bangladesh during monsoon; cool and pleasant in winter
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Luxury eco-resorts in Sylhet outskirts or boutique hotels in city center
travelTips: Rent private country boats with lifejackets for Ratargul swamp
Water shoes recommended for rocky stream beds
destinations.permits_required: None for domestic travelers; border zone caution near Jaflong and Bisnakandi

destinations.name: Sreemangal
destinations.description: Endless hills carpeted with emerald tea bushes, rubber plantations, and the primate-rich canopy of Lawachara National Park.
destinations.weather_notes: Morning fog in winter; vibrant greenery year-round
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Tea estate heritage bungalows and forest cottages
travelTips: Cycle through tea gardens in the early morning
Hire certified forest guard for Lawachara trekking
destinations.permits_required: Park entry ticket for Lawachara and Baikka Beel sanctuary

destinations.name: Sundarbans
destinations.description: A UNESCO World Heritage sanctuary where tidal waterways wind through dense mangrove forests, home to the Royal Bengal tiger, spotted deer, and saltwater crocodiles.
destinations.weather_notes: Pleasant river breeze in winter; calm sea and safe canal cruising
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Cabin accommodation aboard specialized river cruise vessels
travelTips: Always follow armed forest guards on jungle walking trails
Carry binoculars for birdwatching and wildlife spotting
destinations.permits_required: Forest Department entry permit and armed forest guard mandatory

destinations.name: Saint Martin Island
destinations.description: A serene tropical island situated in the southernmost part of Bangladesh, surrounded by turquoise waters, coral reefs, and coconut groves.
destinations.weather_notes: Sunny and breezy in winter; ferry services operate during these months only
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Beachfront eco-resorts and thatched seaside cottages
travelTips: Pre-book sea truck tickets from Teknaf / Cox's Bazar
Respect coral ecosystem and refrain from walking on living coral
destinations.permits_required: Standard ship ticket with passenger travel registration

blogPosts.title: The Ultimate Guide to Sajek Valley: Watching Clouds from Konglak Peak
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything you need to know about traveling to the Kingdom of Clouds — from convoy schedules to best eco-cottages on the ridge.
blogPosts.content:
Sajek Valley is unlike any other destination in Bangladesh. Perched high on the Mizoram border hills, it offers travelers an ethereal spectacle: waking up above a sea of rolling white clouds that lap against mountain ridges like an ocean tide.

### Getting There: The Convoy System
Travel to Sajek begins at Khagrachhari or Dighinala. Due to border geography, all civilian vehicles travel in an organized security convoy twice daily — once at 10:00 AM and again at 3:00 PM. Riding in an open-hood Mahindra 4x4 Chander Gari along the winding hill road is an adventure in itself.

### Where to Stay
The main settlement of Ruilui Para stretches along a narrow mountain ridge. Choose cottages facing east for glorious sunrises over the cloud sea, or west for golden mountain sunsets. Wooden and bamboo cottages provide an authentic, eco-conscious aesthetic with cozy mountain hospitality.

### Must-Do Experiences
1. **Konglak Peak Hike**: A 20-minute steep walk leads to the highest accessible peak in Sajek, offering 360-degree vistas across both Bangladesh and Indian hill ranges.
2. **Tribal Bamboo Chicken**: Sample mountain chicken marinated in forest herbs and slow-cooked inside hollow bamboo stems over charcoal.
3. **Helipad Stargazing**: On clear nights, the Sajek sky transforms into a dazzling celestial canvas free from city light pollution.
blogPosts.author: Tanvir Hasan

blogPosts.title: Into the Mangroves: Field Notes from a 3-Day Sundarbans Cruise
blogPosts.excerpt: Navigating the silent tidal creeks of Kotka and Kachikhali aboard a wooden expedition boat.
blogPosts.content:
The engine cuts out. The only sound left is the rhythmic dip of wooden oars and the distant, haunting cry of an osprey circling the canopy. Welcome to the silent channels of the Sundarbans.

### The World of Sundari and Kewra
The Sundarbans delta is shaped by the twice-daily ebb and flow of high and low tides. Mudskippers scurry across exposed mangrove roots (pneumatophores) that point upward toward the sky like wooden needles. As our silent dinghy glided into a narrow side canal at dawn, three spotted deer paused at the water's edge, watching us with quiet curiosity.

### The Kotka Trail and Jamtola Beach
Landing at Kotka, we followed our armed forest guard along the forest watchtower trail. A clearing in the dense Sundari trees revealed fresh, unmistakable pugmarks pressed into the wet clay — a Bengal tiger had crossed this very clearing less than an hour before us.

Continuing south, the forest abruptly gives way to Jamtola Beach: miles of wild, completely undeveloped coastline where crashing waves meet ancient mangrove driftwood. It is raw, solitary, and magnificent.
blogPosts.author: Raisa Chowdhury

blogPosts.title: Chasing Clear Waters in Sylhet: Ratargul, Sada Pathor & Jaflong
blogPosts.excerpt: Why monsoon in Sylhet turns northeastern Bangladesh into a water wonderland of crystalline streams and flooded forests.
blogPosts.content:
While many travelers avoid traveling during the rainy season, seasoned explorers in Bangladesh know the secret: Sylhet is best experienced during the monsoons.

### Ratargul Freshwater Swamp
One of only a few freshwater swamp forests in South Asia, Ratargul spends four months of the year submerged under 15 to 20 feet of green water. Gliding on a wooden canoe beneath the flooded canopy of Millettia and snake-wood trees feels like stepping into an ancient rainforest from another era.

### Sada Pathor (Bholaganj)
At the northern edge of Sylhet where the Dholai River emerges from the Meghalaya hills, thousands of smooth white limestone boulders lie submerged in crystal-clear mountain water. It has quickly become one of Bangladesh's most sought-after swimming destinations.

### Tips for Traveling Sylhet
- Wear water-friendly sandals with good grip
- Bring waterproof pouches for smartphones and cameras
- Combine Sreemangal and Sylhet into a 4-day combined itinerary for the ultimate nature escape.
blogPosts.author: Mehedi Hasan
